mechanism_revision: V7 falsifies a universal cross-actor consumption claim. State serialization content is behaviorally consequential for Qwen and DeepSeek under the frozen state-only contract, but GLM consumes the local-boundary semantics more conservatively and returns UNKNOWN even when the boundary is explicitly encoded. Persistent-state reliability is therefore a producer-consumer interface problem, not a writer-only serialization problem.
strongest_safe_statement: Typed state stabilizes the written representation on this synthetic package, but behaviorally equivalent use of that state is actor-dependent unless the consumer semantics are also specified or enforced.
method_implication: Future typed-state methods should define both a writer schema and a schema-aware consumer contract. A typed writer alone does not guarantee cross-backbone behavioral equivalence.
next_high_value_step: Design a zero-provider schema-aware consumer contract or deterministic adapter, then prospectively test whether it closes the GLM consumption gap before any real E2 task or heldout use.
